schema_note: Security controls for PACT. Each control names its category, what it does, the source that implements it, the tests that verify it, and the threats it addresses. This is an index; the authoritative description is docs/security.md.

audit_status.note: No independent security audit or certification has been performed. Controls are implemented and tested but not externally reviewed.

controls.control: A missing PACT_AUTH_SECRET refuses every protected request (503); production refuses to start with a missing or short secret.
Signing algorithms are restricted to HS256/HS384/HS512; a misconfigured algorithm fails closed.
Every job access checks party membership; a non-owner gets 404, not 403.
buyer, seller, admin are distinct; reconcile/delete/provider-order require admin.
threats: privilege escalation from a buyer token

controls.control: buyer_id in the request body is overwritten from the token.
Guests are ordinary buyers under a reserved domain; isolation is inherited from ownership checks. Cookie is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Lax, scoped to /api, host-only.
A guest token presented as a bearer header is refused, closing a path around the CSRF check.
Cookie-authenticated mutating requests must echo the session CSRF token in X-CSRF-Token.
Webhook signatures are verified through PayPal's own verify endpoint; an unverifiable event changes nothing.
Each event id is claimed exactly once in a shared store; a duplicate is acknowledged and ignored.
The authorization is claimed and persisted before the provider call; the transition is serialised on the settlement guard (a session advisory lock on PostgreSQL).
Total refunds cannot exceed the captured amount; per-operation idempotency keys; provider refund id dedupe.
A timeout/5xx is AmbiguousOutcome -> job unresolved; never auto-retried; reconcile reads PayPal.
Model verdicts are parsed strictly (as_bool fails closed); verification is a conjunction of deterministic checks and the model verdict.

PACT_PAYPAL_SANDBOX_ONLY refuses a live PayPal host; startup refuses guest sessions against a live host. PAYPAL_ENVIRONMENT must be exactly sandbox or live: any other value is refused at startup in every environment, and paypal.is_live reports true for it, so an ambiguous configuration cannot be presented as a safe sandbox one. GET /api/health reports the resolved environment as paypal.is_live (true only when the config resolves to PayPal's production host), so the guard switch paypal.sandbox_only (off by default) is not mistaken for the deployment's actual environment.
Health and errors expose fixed classifications, never the secret/webhook id/connection string; payer identity is redacted.
Bounded Pydantic models; a 64 KiB body cap enforced on received bytes; a non-finite budget is a 422, not a 500.
PACT_PUBLIC_URL wins for return URLs; otherwise only an allowlisted host is used, so a forged Host cannot redirect the buyer.
Concurrent runs are bounded (semaphore); a run enforces its own deadline and fails the job rather than being killed mid-flight.
SSE tickets are single-use, 60 seconds, single-job, consumed in a shared store.
threats: ticket replay from a captured URL

controls.control: Production refuses to start without DATABASE_URL, so the ledger is durable and the ticket registry is shared.

Every money-bearing route (job create, run, approve, cancel, refund, reconcile, admin provider-order read) is bounded per identity in a fixed window. A guest is keyed on its hashed client address, not its subject, so minting fresh sessions from one address cannot reset the budget. The counter is shared through PostgreSQL when configured; a configured-but-unreachable store refuses every request rather than serving unbounded. Production refuses to start with the guard disabled (PACT_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false).
threats: unbounded provider calls from one caller
provider rate-limit exhaustion for all users
per-address cap evaded by rotating guest sessions
